UPSTREAM: mainboard: Add ASRock H110M-DVS This board is compatible with Intel Skylake and Kaby Lake generation processors. This patch contains the minimum configuration for booting and stable operation of the Ubuntu OS (18.04.1, Linux kernel 4.15). It is based on Intel RVP8 mainboard. Intel Kaby Lake FSP 3.6.0 is used to initialize CPU and PCH. Graphics init with libgfxinit. Works: - Integrated graphics (only DVI port, tested with 1920x1080); - PEG x16 (FSP must be configured with BCT to enable PEG); - all PCIe x1 slots; - all USB and SATA ports; - SuperIO COM port for console; - onboard audio. TODO: - other SuperIO functions; - onboard network chip; - suspend and resume; - documentation. Tested on Intel Core i5-6600 processor with Seabios (rel-1.12.0-10- g171fc89) and Tianocore/edk2 (vUDK2018-8-ge6eccfc) as a payload. BUG=none BRANCH=none TEST=none Change-Id: I2ca40d9a13f62ce23a97b13bdc65d6896f8f9e44 Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: 1217af5e1a83501b4518f29c7f472453681f704d Original-Change-Id: I69396edc50948cf1d0da649241ce92171d32daf7 Original-Signed-off-by: Maxim Polyakov <max.senia.poliak@gmail.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/c/coreboot/+/31603 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Patrick Rudolph <siro@das-labor.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1531582 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

camera: intel: ipu3: Use one stream gfc for video if first time gfc fails BDS (Bayer Down Scaler) and DPC (Defect Pixel Correction) couldn't work together in the IMGU. The Atlas needs to enable the DPC for IQ request, so the BDS must not be used. At the same time, only one stream in video pipe could do YUV scale. So the FOV will not be the same for the two streams in video pipe in some cases. One example in the Atlas: CIO2 outputs: 1920x1080 YUV stream A: 1280x720 YUV stream B: 640x360 For current logic, CIO2 outputs ==(IMGU YUV crop)==> 1280x720 (stream A) CIO2 outputs ==(IMGU YUV scale)==> 640x360 (stream B) So it has FOV issue. After this patch, only one stream is enabled for video pipe. CIO2 outputs ==(IMGU YUV scale)==> 1280x720 (stream A) 1280x720 (stream A) ==(SW scale)==> 640x360 (stream B) It trys to use the normal graph config settings, so it requests two streams from IMGU for the above case. If it fails which means there is no normal graph config settings, it will try to use one stream graph config setting, and the setting will be provided in the Atlas. So it needs the Atlas to delete the unwanted gfc settings and have one stream graph config settings. BUG=b:122905372 TEST=Build and deploy package to platform, camera works and CTS passes. Change-Id: Iccd5da73ca9112ce017451f3ee5aac891b16bd3a Signed-off-by: Yang Liang <liang.l.yang@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1423520 Commit-Ready: Wei Meng <wei.meng@intel.com> Tested-by: Wei Meng <wei.meng@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Hung-yu Wu <hywu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Wei Meng <wei.meng@intel.com>

system_api: Constant for file name that marks device as locked to single user This defines the name of a temporary file. The file will be created by cryptohome when request comes to lock the device to a single user, if it manages to successfully do the cryptohome operation (i.e extending PCR). The presence of the file will be used by login_manager to reboot the device on sign out if the file is present. Also homedirs will use the existence of the file to know which vault keyset to use in decryption. The above could also be achieved by reading the PCR when needed, but this saves us from a trip to TPM on every login/sign out, and keeps the code simple. The file disappears on shutdown, which is in line with needed functionality. driver: lsm6dsm: Fix race condition and sensor labeling issues This commit fixes two issues with the LSM6DSM driver: - it fixes a race condition in load_fifo() which could lead to samples being labeled at the wrong timestamp if the FIFO was cleared, and a new interrupt occurred, between reading the last sample, and pushing it to the motion sense queue - it drops samples even when the ODR is changed to the same final normalized rate, since the sensor is turned off/on regardless of this condition; additionally, it adds one more sample to the number of samples to be discarded, since I was experimentally seeing occasional spurious data in the first sample after a rate change. tast: Use en-US for VirtualKeyboardSuggestions. Previously this test failed on devices with a Japanese keyboard, where the input method defaults to "Japanese Keyboard". This keyboard does not have suggestions so the test failed. We change the test to always switch to the en-US input method so that this test can run on any devices. Future plan is to test all the supported Chrome OS languages in this test.
